news.title: Malawi’s Women Made World Cup History. Can That Attention Turn Into Arrivals?
news.lede: Temwa Chawinga was already one of the biggest names in American women’s soccer before this summer. The Kansas City Current forward has won the NWSL Golden Boot and MVP award in back-to-back seasons, becoming the first player in league history to win consecutive MVP titles. Her older sister, Tabitha, captains Malawi and plays for OL Lyonnes after a career that has taken her through Sweden, China, Milan, and Paris. This summer, what changed was the national team around them.

news.title: Justin Bieber, Shakira, BTS and Madonna will not be paid for World Cup final half time show
news.lede: The halftime show might also break FIFA's own rules. Much like at the Super Bowl, the headliners at the World Cup final halftime show will not be paid for their performances - but for a different reason. Justin Bieber, Shakira, Madonna, Burna Boy, and BTS are among the huge names performing in the 11-minute show in front of tens of thousands of fans at the MetLife Stadium, as well as being broadcast to millions around the world. The final is scheduled for 19 July, with the halftime show being the first such performance to happen at a FIFA World Cup, being curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin.

news.title: Sophie Cunningham’s football kick goes wrong in front of hundreds at NASCAR race
news.lede: Sophie Cunningham made her presence felt at the NASCAR Cup Series race. The Indiana Fever star was in Madison, Illinois, for Sunday’s Enjoy Illinois 300, and she hardly stayed in the background. But a moment on stage quickly became the highlight of her visit for a very different reason, as her athleticism did not exactly shine during a football kicking attempt. Cunningham is known as a basketball player, but she also has experience with football.

news.lede: That's according to European football journalists Kevin Hatchard and Andy Brassell as they sit winless at the bottom of Spain's top flight. After their 1-0 defeat to Sevilla on Friday night, Valencia have just one point to show for their efforts with five matches played in LaLiga. Carlos Corberan, formerly in charge of Championship side West Brom, has been sacked as head coach of his boyhood club amid their poor run. Ex-Chelsea chief Ron Gourlay has also been dismissed from his role as CEO of Football at Valencia, who were crowned Spanish champions in the 2003/04 season.

news.title: Why the upcoming international break is three weeks as England play four games
news.lede: Previously, there were four breaks of two-week windows during the Premier League season – in September, October, November and March, followed by a June international window. This format saw each country play two matches per window, but that is all set to change this year. Instead of separate breaks in September and October, there will now be a three-week gap for international fixtures across late September and early October, with the two windows merging. Countries will play four matches across two weeks as opposed to the traditional two matches in a week format.

news.title: World Cup dreams take shape for Oman’s U15s
news.lede: MUSCAT: Oman’s Under-15 football team has begun its first training camp in Muscat, with 22 players competing for 14 places at the inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival in Azerbaijan from October 22 to 31. The camp, running from September 12 to 17, brings together players identified through the youth league and a scouting process at clubs outside the competition. It gives the coaching staff its first opportunity to assess the group before choosing the squad that will represent Oman at the new Fifa event.Team manager Khalid al Wahaibi said the selection process began with players observed in the youth league. The staff then visited clubs and arranged assessment sessions for their players, spending approximately a week with different groups before settling on the initial 22-man list.“.

news.title: Westfield Resident To Represent U.S. In 2026 Transplant Football World Cup
news.lede: WESTFIELD, NJ — More than a decade after receiving a liver transplant, Westfield resident Matt Felix is set to represent the United States at the 2026 Transplant Football World Cup in Frankfurt, Germany. The tournament is scheduled for Sept. 13 to 18 and is hosted by the World Transplant Games Federation. It brings together transplant recipient athletes from around the world. Felix, a longtime advocate for NJ Sharing Network, said the trip is about more than soccer.
